summary:
Our project was created with the purpose of developing an innovative solution to address challenges affecting our planet through science, technology, and space exploration. By using digital tools, data analysis, and scientific resources provided by NASA, we aim to transform information into valuable knowledge that helps us better understand the problems affecting our environment.

This initiative focuses on combining creativity, research, and technology to design a functional, accessible, and socially valuable solution. Throughout its development, we aim to identify a problem, investigate its causes, analyze available data, and create a technological solution that contributes to addressing it. Furthermore, the project encourages learning, collaboration, and critical thinking, demonstrating that younger generations can contribute meaningful ideas to global challenges.

Our ultimate goal is to create a positive impact, encourage interest in science and innovation, and demonstrate how knowledge related to space exploration can be applied to improve life on Earth.
details:
Our project is based on the creation of a video game and a virtual museum with the purpose of raising awareness about the equipment abandoned by NASA in space.

The Video Game

The game is based on real-life missions. It consists of a simulation that gives users the experience of being an astronaut stranded in space who must solve different problems by collecting equipment (space debris) left behind by NASA.

Each mission (level) represents a real mission carried out by one of these pieces of equipment. At the beginning of each level, users are provided with general information to help them complete the mission while also gaining knowledge. As the game progresses, interesting facts appear through pop-up windows. Users must try to memorize this information in order to be prepared for the quiz at the end of each mission, ensuring that learning takes place effectively.

It is also important to highlight that the game will be connected to satellite data so that the information remains constantly updated.

We also intend to establish partnerships with the Ministry of Education so that students can access the platform using their institutional email accounts and select their educational institution. This will allow us to create an annual school ranking that encourages healthy competition and promotes knowledge about space. Through this initiative, we hope to capture the interest of both students and the general public.

The project offers several benefits, such as making learning more engaging, enjoyable, and interactive. As we all know, today's generation is increasingly attracted to dynamic and interactive experiences, such as video games, rather than traditional learning methods like reading books.

The expected impact is to revolutionize the way these topics are taught by motivating students through an innovative learning experience and friendly competition.

To develop this video game, we used Python programming, with the assistance of Google's AI in the development process.

Our project is creative because we conducted a series of surveys to understand why students lose interest in these subjects. We discovered that many students consider them boring or find the language used difficult to understand. Based on these findings, we decided to combine something they usually find boring with something they genuinely enjoy. That is how we came up with this innovative idea.

We also took into consideration that many students do not avoid participating because they are poor students, but rather because they lack support from their educational institutions and face difficulties when trying to carry out projects of this kind.

The Virtual Museum

The virtual museum is a space dedicated entirely to knowledge. It is designed to serve as a secondary learning resource after students develop curiosity and a desire to learn more about the subject through the game.

In this space, users will find all the information they need about the missions carried out. This includes everything from the objective of each mission to its exact location, obtained through satellite data collected by radar systems.

The museum will also be connected to satellite data to ensure that its information remains up to date. Additionally, it will feature a language selection button, offering English and Spanish (for now).

One of its main benefits is that all the information is gathered in one place, saving users the time and effort of researching each mission separately.

We hope students will take advantage of the resources provided, allowing their imagination and knowledge to grow.

Part of the museum's code was developed by our team, while the remaining part was developed with the assistance of Google's AI.

The project is creative because, according to our research, there is no existing museum quite like this one. It is an innovative idea that makes accessing information significantly easier and more convenient for users.

We also took into consideration that students do not stop getting involved because they are poor students, but because they often lack support from their educational institutions and face challenges when trying to develop projects of this kind.

The Apollo 11 Lunar Module (LM) "Eagle" was the first crewed vehicle to land on the Moon. It carried two astronauts, Commander Neil A. Armstrong and LM pilot Edwin E. "Buzz" Aldrin, Jr., the first men to walk on the Moon. Also included on the LM was the Early Apollo Scientific Experiment Package (EASEP), which consisted of several self-contained experiments to be deployed and left on the lunar surface, and other scientific and sample collection apparatus.

The Apollo 15 lunar module (LM) "Falcon" was the fourth crewed vehicle to land on the Moon. It carried two astronauts, Commander David R. Scott and LM pilot James B. Irwin, the seventh and eighth men to walk on the Moon. The LM also carried a Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV), an Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP) that contained scientific experiments to be deployed and left on the lunar surface, and other scientific and sample collection apparatus. The experiments performed on the Moon, in addition to the ALSEP suite, were geologic sample collection, surface photography, soil mechanics investigations to study physical properties of the lunar regolith, and the solar wind composition experiment which collected samples of solar wind particles for return to Earth.
